newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Sainsbury focus now on basics.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Sainsbury focus now on basics.

text.p: J. Sainsbury Plc chairman David Sainsbury said he thought the focus would be on basics this year and improving profits next year.
"I think this year will be about getting the basics right, next year will be about getting profits moving," he told Reuters in a telephone interview.
The supermarket retailer said earlier that first-half pretax profits slipped to 393 million stg from 456 million stg last time and is to pay a dividend of 3.5 pence, up from 3.4 pence.
David Sainsbury said the company wanted to improve current sales growth, which has seen like-for-like sales growth keeping pace with inflation at around three percent.
"Clearly we want to do better than that," he said.
He added that marketing and operations initiatives along with the group's new Reward loyalty card should help to boost sales between now and Christmas.
Sainsbury had said earlier in its results statement that it was expecting "strong" Christmas trading season.
"We will be fighting on our traditional ground of quality and choice, along with customer loyalty," David Sainsbury said.
He said the group's new management team should help to improve operational and marketing performance.

Dino Adriano, deputy chief executive of the supermarkets business, will now take over as chief executive of the division from Tom Vyner on March 8 instead of a previously scheduled move at the end of next year.
David Sainsbury said the impact of a petrol price war had seen a swing of 24 million stg between profits on the business in the first half of last year and the loss this year.
But he said petrol was now "back to breakeven and if that holds it will help us going forward."
The group should also benefit from new store openings, he added, as it increases sales area by 6.4 percent.
"That will be an enormous help in driving forward market share," David Sainsbury said.
Despite the poor like-for-like sales performance, Sainsbury said it improved market share to 12.5 percent in the first half from 12.3 percent a year ago.
David Sainsbury said the group's plans to set up a bank with Bank of Scotland, announced last week, were not seen "as something that will transform our basic operations."
But he said banking facilities at stores would "meet a real customer need."
